hypothesis: Annualized increments in mean measured stature, computed from age-specific cross-sectional means, are highest in infancy, fall to a low and roughly constant plateau in mid-childhood, rise to a second maximum in the early teens, and then fall to near zero by the late teens.
pass_criterion: Using pooled NHANES cycles, computed separately for boys and girls with survey weights, let v(a) be the annualized change in weighted mean height between adjacent 1-year age bins (recumbent length under 2 years, standing height from 2 years). The claim passes only if all four hold in both sexes: (1) mean v over ages 0.5-2 is at least 1.5 times mean v over ages 5-9; (2) v across ages 5-9 is steady, with max minus min no more than 40% of its mean; (3) the pubertal peak, max v over ages 9-15, is at least 1.25 times mean v over ages 5-9, and falls at age 10-13 in girls and 11-15 in boys; (4) mean v over ages 17-20 is below 1.0 cm/yr and below 20% of the pubertal peak.
fail_criterion: The claim fails if, in either sex, any one of the four conditions is violated. In particular it fails if the pubertal peak is less than 1.1 times the mid-childhood mean v, if infancy v is not at least 1.2 times mid-childhood v, or if v over ages 17-20 stays at or above 1.0 cm/yr.
interpretation: "Curve of growth for length or stature" is read as the velocity curve, meaning height gained per year. Thompson's "rapid increase at the outset" is infancy (0-2 y). "Slower, almost steady growth in early boyhood" is ages 5-9. "Marked quickening in his teens" is the pubertal growth spurt. "Gradual arrest" is the approach to adult height. Thompson wrote about boys. Girls are tested as well, and their spurt is expected earlier. NHANES is cross-sectional, so velocity is inferred from differences between successive age-bin means, not from individual longitudinal growth. This is a modern reinterpretation. Secular trends and cohort differences could blur the spurt, so the peak is judged on bins no wider than 1 year. NHANES gives measured recumbent length for young children and measured standing height from age 2. The fields used would be RIDAGEYR or RIDAGEEX, RIAGENDR, BMXRECUM, BMXHT and the WTMEC survey weights.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US CDC National Center for Health Statistics
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES publicly releases measured (not self-reported) recumbent length and standing height for people from infancy to old age, by age and sex, with survey weights. That allows weighted mean height by age, and hence annualized increments across infancy, childhood, adolescence and early adulthood. The Examination Body Measures files and the Demographics files can be downloaded as SAS transport files.
